text:
lena: Proposal: introduce an 'atomic-flip window' for high-risk flags. Instead of an immediate wide flip, we publish a scheduled atomic swap with a short guarded window (e.g., 30s) where we monitor and can instant-rollback via an escrowed approval token. Goal: make large flips observable and abortable with low blast radius.

josh: Curious how this differs from canary + rollout. Is atomic-flip targeted at flags that must change across many replicas simultaneously (e.g., model weight updates)?
lena: Exactly. Some flags require coordinated swap (routing tables, model versions). Canary doesn't cut it because partial state causes correctness issues. Atomic-flip ensures either all nodes flip in the window or we revert quickly.
ravi: How is the guard enforced? If we flip many nodes at once, we risk synchronous load spikes. Need pre-checks and a quick fallback path.
lena: Plan: runtime performs a two-phase commit: 1) publish 'prepare' with checksum; 2) execute swap at T0 across nodes within a bounded window; 3) monitor SLOs and telemetry for T0..T0+window and auto-rollback if thresholds exceeded.
maya: UX: Console should show a scheduled timeline, an "abort" button active until T0+window end, and an escrow panel showing who holds override tokens. Also provide a dry-run to show which nodes would flip.
devon: Telemetry/alerts: suggest metrics config.flip_attempts, config.flip_success, config.flip_rollback, config.flip_latency_spike. Alert on flip_rollback > 0 or flip_latency_spike > 10% p95 vs baseline in the window.
cara: SRE: For infra-critical flips default mode = fail-closed on failure (rollback). For low-risk flips allow auto-fallback to compatible variant. Need an oncall safemode token to cancel or force-complete with audit trail.
priya: Approval flow idea: escrow tokens are created at schedule time and assigned to owners + a secondary approver (2-person rule). Tokens are short-lived and must be used to override automatic rollback. Overrides require justification string recorded in audit.
josh: Implementation note: two-phase commit across many nodes can stall. Use a soft-sync: each node applies locally at T0, reports success, and runtime quorum decides commit vs rollback. Keep messages minimal to avoid network storms.
ravi: What about rollback behavior? Should rollback be a symmetric swap or a fallback route to an older model endpoint? Symmetric rollback may reintroduce the original problem.
lena: Option: rollback policy per-flag: symmetric_swap | route_fallback | graceful_degrade. Default to route_fallback for heavy infra changes.
maya: Console copy: when schedule is pending show clear human-friendly explanation, probable impact, and a checklist: preflight green, telemetry bound set, owners assigned. Provide one-click link to open a dry-run report.
devon: Preflight should enforce telemetry presence: require at least one of flip_rollback or flip_latency_spike bound and autocreate a dashboard stub if missing. configbot should fail preflight if no SLOs attached.
configbot: preflight check: schema OK. WARNING: missing telemetry bindings for flip_rollback. Recommend auto-provisioning dashboard /dashboards/flags/2829001111-atomic-flip.
cara: Runbook stub: 1) if auto-rollback triggered, notify oncall and owners; 2) gather timeline and affected nodes; 3) if rollback insufficient, invoke safemode token to re-run with adjusted parameters; 4) open postmortem if rollback_count > 1.
josh: Perf/coordination: nodes should apply swap with a jitter window (e.g., 0-200ms) to avoid lockstep IO spikes, but still be within the observable window. Need tests for clock skew and partition scenarios.
priya: Security: escrow tokens are HSM-backed and appear in audit logs. Override UI should require MFA and two approvers. Also automatic email to product/security on any override.
ravi: Edge-case: partial network partition where only subset flips and quorum can't be reached. System should choose safe default (per-flag policy) and notify.
lena: Action items: lena -> RFC + sample atomic-flip config; josh -> two-phase commit sketch + jitter tests; devon -> telemetry bounds and alert templates; cara -> runbook + safemode token playbook; maya -> Console mocks and copy; priya -> approval/escrow security design.
configbot: reminder: create RFC under /eng/flags/rfcs and attach preflight id 2829001111.
lena: thanks team — want a quick PoC before next retro :rocket:
